what: Diageo is the world's largest spirits company. It owns Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Tanqueray, Captain Morgan, Baileys, Don Julio and Guinness, and sells in almost every country.
customers: Bars, restaurants, supermarkets, duty-free retailers and distributors worldwide.
money: US spirits, led by whisky and tequila
moat: Brands people ask for by name, aged whisky stocks laid down decades ago that no new entrant can replicate, and global distribution.
risks: US spirits demand has been weak as consumers trade down
Inventory built up at distributors had to be worked off, hurting shipments
Debt of about $24 billion against $2 billion of cash
Younger drinkers in several markets are drinking less
opportunities: Tequila and Guinness have both been growing while the rest of the portfolio has not
Cost-cutting targets have been raised to protect margins
Aged whisky stock becomes more valuable the longer it sits
watch: Organic sales growth in the United States and whether distributor inventories have normalised.
